summary: Four requests were reviewed against intake/requests (ver_0mwgs1r1z0g838a7bf8). Three of them (syn-req-001, syn-req-003, syn-req-004) share one need: a single, reusable dataset freshness capability with policy-configured thresholds that reports fresh, stale, or unknown. syn-req-002 asks for schema-contract drift checking, which is a different check type, so it is listed as unrelated to this capability and flagged for a scope decision. No files were written. The analysis was done by reading the pinned request text; no tools or data sources were queried.

criteria_claims.note: shared_capability is named in one sentence. Each of the three consolidated requests (001, 003, 004) has its own distinct_needs entry in its own terms. syn-req-002 is listed as unrelated with a reason. Checked by reading the JSON document in artifacts. No tools were run.

observed_facts only restate request text with ids. Interpretations are labeled as inference. Unknowns are listed, and the decision-level ones are also asked of chief_of_staff in questions[]. Checked by reading the document. No tools were run.

remaining_uncertainty: Whether syn-req-002 belongs in this capability is a scope decision that the requests do not settle.
Threshold values for NCR tables and the policy owner are not stated.
The data sources for freshness timestamps and the NCR table list are unverified; no data was inspected.

questions.question: Should syn-req-002 (schema contract drift by field) be folded into the same shared capability as the freshness requests (001, 003, 004), or kept as a separate capability that can reuse the same policy and reporting layer later?
Who owns and approves the freshness threshold policy values (for example, the 60-minute threshold for engine_test_runs and the thresholds for NCR tables)?
Which NCR tables are in scope for syn-req-003, and what is the authoritative source for owner-team mapping?
